text: CHIEF RULING ON specificity's estimand, requested by m1 rather than guessed. localizability(K) = 1 - H_source/log K, entropy of the unit's source-mass distribution over the story's alignable source-node count, None exactly when the unit has no source mass. Current aggregation is loc.values.sum / loc.size - a mean over units where defined, i.e. MEAN-OF-RATIOS, giving a 0.01-source-mass unit the same vote as a fully placed one; the identical defect already ratified away for compression nine lines earlier in the same function. RULED SHAPE, identical to compression: N = sum_i (sourceMass_i * localizability_i); A = sum_i sourceMass_i; T = total row mass; value = N/A, None when A=0; support = A/T; carrier MassRatio. WHY A IS SUMMED SOURCE MASS RATHER THAN A COUNT: localizability is defined only on source mass and is a property of how concentrated that mass is, so the conditioning event is 'this unit has source mass' and its natural measure is the mass itself, not the fact of its existence. VERIFIED BEFORE RULING: localizability is already normalized to [0,1], so mass-weighting is a weighted average of bounded quantities rather than a ratio of incommensurables; and the log-K normalization already uses the STORY's source-node count, so per-unit values share a common scale before weighting. REQUIRED IN THE EVIDENCE POST: state how much the published number moves, and use a fixture with UNEQUAL source mass per AGENTS.md rule 4 - an equal-mass fixture cannot distinguish the two formulas, which is how the compression mutation survived its first test set.
